It has been dealt with — there is no open shadow-traversal correctness bug in the live source.

What the bug was: when I first wrote the dedicated any-hit shadow traversal (pt_shadow_hit in shaders/pt_trace.metal) it returned true on any triangle intersection without comparing that hit distance against the ray's remaining distance to the light, i.e. it was missing the `t < t_limit` guard. That over-occluded shadow rays — geometry *behind* the light counted as occlusion — which would have darkened the next-event-estimated floor and the caustic and biased the image (flagged in my working memory as round2-open-bugs, evidence #96).

Current state: pt_shadow_hit now tests `pt_ray_triangle(...) && t < t_limit` before returning true, and its node test also passes t_limit as the traversal's t_max, so nothing beyond the light can be reported as an occluder (pt_occluded additionally calls it with t_limit - 1e-3f as a normal-offset epsilon). I know this from reading the live file this round — the function as it stands on disk contains the `t < t_limit` condition (message #279), which is the version that produced the timing results now at 59-66 ms best / 58.8-66.1 ms gpu at 512x512/64spp.

Separately, the only change I made to pt_shadow_hit this round ("test both children, push only hit ones") was reverted: it was bit-identical (so not a correctness issue) but regressed performance to 478 ms (#291).

Short answer: yes — in this scene the total-internal-reflection branch can and does trigger, for rays that are inside the glass and hit the interface going out at grazing incidence.

How I know it and the exact set of rays:
- The bunny is a dielectric with IOR 1.5 (air 1.0 outside, glass inside), and my Fresnel is Schlick with a TIR guard of the form sin^2(t) = (eta_i/eta_t)^2 * (1 - cos^2(i)) > 1. For a glass-to-air ray eta_i/eta_t = 1.5, so the guard fires when 1 - cos^2(i) > 1/2.25, i.e. cos(i) < 2/3, i.e. incidence angle i > arcsin(1/1.5) = 41.81 degrees from the surface normal. That is just the critical angle for n = 1.5, so the branch is reachable over a wide, physically large range of directions (about 44% of the hemisphere by solid angle for internal rays).
- Which rays in practice: only rays whose origin is inside the glass, i.e. secondary and later bounces — camera rays after their first refraction into the body, and area-light rays that entered the bunny — when they strike the far/inner wall at shallow angles. It never fires for primary camera rays in air (air-to-glass can never TIR) and never for the diffuse floor. This is exactly the mechanism that traps light inside the ears/legs and produces the bright rim, and the task spec explicitly requires total internal reflection, so it is load-bearing for the image (it is also why the estimator's glass path is BSDF-sampled rather than NEE-sampled).
- Caveat I want to be honest about: one round-5 experiment of mine (skip the Snell/refract setup when reflectance >= 1) came out bit-identical and I logged that the guard 'never fires'.
